SMALL STEPS. WORKING VERSIONS.

From “what if”
to what's next.

Build with a little guidance
  1. 01 / FRAME IT

    Give the idea context.

    Describe the person, the problem, and the first useful thing your product should do.

  2. 02 / BUILD IT

    Make one clear change.

    Codex works inside your project. Follow its activity and keep the task small enough to review.

  3. 03 / CHECK IT

    Look at the actual result.

    Read the changed files, run project checks, and try the interaction in the preview.

  4. 04 / MAKE IT YOURS

    Keep the next version close.

    Your files and run history stay with the project. Come back with the next useful change.

A FEW USEFUL DETAILS

Before you begin.

Are Vibe One and Vibe Law different products?+

They are distinct offerings on one platform. Vibe One supports general building; Vibe Law is focused on legal technology. You manage access to each offering through the same account.

Where does the Workbench fit?+

The Workbench is your signed-in account and project area. Project Studio keeps briefs and files organised. Practice is where you edit and build projects. The original Design Studio stays available alongside them.

What do I need to build with Codex?+

Start the local companion and sign in to the official Codex CLI on your computer. This version uses that signed-in subscription. Claude and API keys are not enabled.

Download the local companion
Is this a paid subscription?+

This release offers free local trial access. It does not collect payment or create a paid subscription. The account area explains which offerings are active for you.

Where are my projects stored?+

Your project files, account data and build history are stored by the local companion on your computer. Starting a Codex task shares the task and relevant project context with Codex. The hosted frontend requires the local companion to build.
